chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Urama from one of his companions from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Fudayl from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is a brother to the believer of his father and his mother, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the believers from the clay of the Gardens, and caused to flow into their forms from the wind of Paradise; therefore, they are brothers of a father and a mother.'

key_terms.رِيحِ الْجَنَّةِ: Wind of Paradise (symbolizing divine breath or spirit)
key_terms.طِينَةِ الْجِنَانِ: Clay of the Gardens (referring to the spiritual substance of Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual basis for the brotherhood between believers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the metaphysical basis of believer's kinship, tracing it to a shared spiritual essence created from the 'clay of the Gardens' and infused with the 'wind of Paradise.' This hadith, found in Al-Kafi, elevates the bond of faith beyond social ties to a divine ontological connection, reinforcing the concept of *Ukhuwwah* (brotherhood) as a reflection of shared spiritual origin. It underscores the Shia understanding that the believer's soul is intrinsically linked to the divine realm, making mutual love and loyalty a religious obligation rooted in creation itself.
